public_health_question.v: What were the clinical features and outcomes of severe Bartonella quintana infections among persons experiencing unsheltered homelessness in New York City?

ev.q: Severe Bartonella quintana Infections Among Persons Experiencing Unsheltered Homelessness — New York City
Four patients received a diagnosis of culture-negative, left-sided endocarditis and underwent surgical valve replacement
DOHMH conducted retrospective active surveillance within clinical laboratories of five large NYC hospital networks to identify additional cases
reviewed electronic medical records of all identified patients
Housing status was determined from the medical record or the NYC Department of Homeless Services (DHS) system.

equity.level_reason: Unsheltered homelessness (SES) defines the population of a six-case series; no group comparison by an SPD is made.

determinants_of_health.v: homelessness; limited access to hygiene facilities

ev.q: homelessness is the principal risk factor for B. quintana infection ( 2 ), likely attributable to limited access to hygiene facilities

notes: Case series of six patients identified by retrospective laboratory case finding; design named as surveillance but read as a case series.
